subject: Shortfall coverage credit — request for VP/CFO exception
messages:
From: Bryan Patel <bryan@healthquant.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Shortfall coverage request for Q4 ramp

Tessa —

Quick note on our Q4 ramp: we committed to ~250M tokens for the initial pilot but due to a delayed data ingestion window and a pushed-back integration milestone, we're tracking at ~150M tokens (roughly 60%) for the period that was supposed to hit the commitment. Our execs are worried that the gap will materially change the commercial calculus for the program.

Ask: can Redwood provide a one-time "shortfall coverage" credit to bridge the delta so we can keep the pilot timeline intact? We can commit to a 12-month extension (starting when integration is complete) in exchange for a credit that covers the difference for the current quarter.

Attached: weekly-usage.csv (summary by day)

Happy to chat if easier — Bryan
Senior Product Lead, HealthQuant
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Bryan Patel <bryan@healthquant.com>
Cc: Alice Nguyen <alice@healthquant.com>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Shortfall coverage request for Q4 ramp

Bryan —

Thanks for the note and the usage sheet. I’m sorry to hear about the integration delays — we want to avoid letting that derail the pilot. We have two pragmatic options that might work:

1) One-time shortfall credit: Redwood issues a $120,000 credit to cover the delta for Q4, applied to the next invoice. In return, HealthQuant signs a 12-month committed usage extension at current rates.

2) Blended concession + term: 20% concession for the remainder of the quarter + a 12-month extension with a modest usage minimum. Reduces immediate cash impact for both sides.

I’ll need to run either option up for VP/CFO signoff because both exceed our delegated discount authority. Can you confirm (a) whether HealthQuant is willing to sign a 12-month extension and (b) if billing can switch to net-30 auto-charge on the new term? If yes I’ll push an approval memo to our finance and sales leadership today.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: INTERNAL: HQ-2026-069 — request for shortfall coverage credit (VP/CFO approval requested)

Team —

Need a quick exec signoff on a one-time shortfall coverage concession for HealthQuant (deal HQ-2026-069). Below are the facts and the ask.

Summary:
- Committed pilot tokens: 250M for Q4 (signed PoC addendum)
- Actual usage to date: ~150M (weekly-usage.csv attached)
- Delta: ~100M tokens (~$120k revenue gap using current consumption rates)

Commercial proposal (two possible tracks):
A) Straight credit: issue $120,000 one-time credit to cover the Q4 shortfall. Condition: HealthQuant signs 12-month extension at current rates (start date = contract amendment execution).
B) Split approach: $70,000 immediate credit + a 12-month extension with a 15% minimum usage floor (protects unit economics).

Impact (conservative estimates):
- A reduces recognized ARR this quarter by ~$120k but preserves relationship and upsell potential; 12-month extension expected to recover ~1.8x the one-time concession in revenue over 12 months based on forecasted uptake.
- B reduces immediate hit to $70k and provides greater revenue protection via floor.

Risk notes / controls requested:
- Credit only applied after DocuSign amendment countersigned and auto-billing set to net-30; no retroactive refunds.
- Legal to approve amendment language; finance to amend billing schedule.
- Limit: this approval request exceeds T&E delegated discount authority and should be treated as an exception memo.

Attachments: pricing_model_v3.xlsx (forecast w/ and w/o concession), weekly-usage.csv
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/54621/HQ-2026-069

Request: Marissa, can you authorize the $120k one-time credit (option A) or suggest the max approval threshold? Jonas/Grace — do you support option A or B? Need a decision by EOD 11/11 to keep HealthQuant on schedule.

Thanks — Tessa
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: HQ-2026-069 — request for shortfall coverage credit (VP/CFO approval requested)

Tessa—

Thanks for the clear memo. A few follow-up items before I can sign off:
1) Can you quantify the expected net present value (NPV) impact of the one-time $120k credit vs. the projected recovery from the 12-month extension (we should use conservative uptake assumptions)? Please put numbers in pricing_model_v3.xlsx and highlight the downside scenario.
2) Confirm whether the credit will be recognized as contra-revenue in the current quarter or as a billing adjustment (we prefer contra-revenue treatment for transparency).
3) Legal needs to confirm amendment language that protects Redwood from early termination during the extension term.

If the NPV looks reasonable (>= 1.5x recovery over 12 months on conservative uptake) and Legal signs off, I’m prepared to approve the $120k one-time credit on the condition that the term extension and auto-billing requirements are met.

Marissa Cole
VP, Finance — Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: HQ-2026-069 — request for shortfall coverage credit (VP/CFO approval requested)

+1 to Marissa's conditions. Sales supports option A subject to the following guardrails:
- Credit cap at $120k (no incremental concessions).
- Amendment must include a 12-month committed term and a 15% usage floor (Jonas to approve any deviation).
- Finance to hold first invoice until DocuSign is fully executed; apply credit on next invoice after execution.

Assuming those are in place, I recommend approving the $120k credit — it protects the customer relationship and keeps the deal on a path to recovery/expansion.

Jonas Weber
Head of Enterprise Sales
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Bryan Patel <bryan@healthquant.com>, Alice Nguyen <alice@healthquant.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2026 17:45:00 -0800
Subject: Shortfall coverage credit — conditional approval and next steps

Bryan / Alice —

Thanks for your patience. Internal approval path has cleared with conditions. Summary of the outcome:

- Approved: one-time shortfall coverage credit of $120,000 (applies to Q4 shortfall)
- Conditions: HealthQuant signs a 12-month extension amendment (DocuSign link below) and agrees to net-30 auto-billing. Amendment must include a 15% minimum usage floor; credit applied only after countersignature.

Next steps:
1) I’ve attached the draft term-sheet (docsign-term-sheet.pdf) and opened the DocuSign envelope: https://www.docusign.com/unsigned/HQ-2026-069-term-sheet
2) Once countersigned, Finance will apply the $120,000 credit to your next invoice as a contra-revenue adjustment and we’ll confirm updated billing schedule.
3) Legal will insert language to protect Redwood from early termination during the extended term; Tessa will share final amendment copy.

I’ll be available to walk your team through the amendment if helpful. Appreciate you working with us on a pragmatic solution.

— Tessa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
